title: The rising food prices are attributed to a combination of factors, including poor harvests, increased biofuel production, and lower food reserves. A significant portion of food crops, particularly maize, is being redirected to biofuels, leading to reduced food availability for human consumption. While some analysts argue that global population growth is a contributing factor to the food crisis, others point out that grain availability has outpaced population growth. Additionally, rising crude oil prices have increased fertilizer costs, further impacting food production. The situation is particularly dire for those living at subsistence levels, who struggle to afford food as prices rise.
